meta.title: Wolter Invest — Own the assets, earn a share of net profit
meta.description: Wolter is a battery-swap and e-bike network in Tashkent. Through Islamic finance (Ijarah), own physical assets and earn a share of monthly net profit. Asset-backed, not equity.

hero.lead: Wolter operates a battery-swap network and e-bikes in Tashkent. You finance and own the assets; we operate and share the profit.
hero.disclaimer: These figures are illustrative projections based on current pilot run-rate. Returns depend on actual net profit and are not guaranteed.

problem.title: The battery is a courier's biggest barrier.
problem.subtitle: Three things cap a courier's income:

cards.title: Charging time
cards.text: Charging a battery takes hours — the courier can't work meanwhile and income stops.

cards.title: Battery cost
cards.text: Owning a battery is a large outlay. Many couriers can't afford it.

cards.title: Downtime
cards.text: A dead or broken battery means no orders, no income. A direct loss.

market.title: The delivery economy is growing — couriers need reliable power.

cards.title: 📈 Delivery boom
cards.text: E-commerce and food delivery are growing fast in Tashkent — courier numbers and daily trips keep rising.

cards.title: ⚡ Shift to electric
cards.text: The shift from petrol motorcycles to e-bikes is accelerating — charge and downtime remain the main barrier.

cards.title: 🔋 Battery economics
cards.text: The swap model cuts downtime to zero and turns a large cost into a manageable monthly fee.

market.note: Exact market-size figures (TAM/SAM) are being validated by independent research — no estimated market numbers are shown on this page.

structure.title: You own the asset — we operate.

steps.title: Finance
steps.text: You finance the asset pool (on an ijara basis).

steps.title: Ownership
steps.text: All hardware is your property for the term — in your name.

steps.title: Operate
steps.text: Wolter deploys to couriers, maintains and markets.

steps.title: Income
steps.text: 70% until payback, then 30% of net profit through month 48.

structure.phase1: Until payback: 70% of monthly net profit to the investor — capital returns on an accelerated basis.
structure.phase2: From payback to month 48: 30% to the investor — pure net profit.
structure.iqtino: At the end of 4 years, assets transfer to Wolter (lease-to-own).
structure.islomText: The structure is designed to conform to Islamic-finance principles — an Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek (lease-to-own) model, aligned with AAOIFI Standard No. 9. The asset is held in the investor's name, ownership risk is borne by the investor, and iqtino is formalized via a separate promise.

ownership.title: What exactly you own — and what protects you.

cards.title: 🏷️ What you own
cards.text: Physical assets (cabinet, e-bike, battery) are registered in your name. Not equity — income-producing property via ijara.

cards.title: 🛰️ If Wolter stops
cards.text: The asset stays yours. Each cabinet has GPS and remote control — location and status are tracked.

cards.title: ↗️ Exit / transfer
cards.text: The asset can be leased to another operator, sold, or the network transferred. Under iqtino, ownership passes to Wolter at month 48.

ownership.note: Insurance, custody and asset-registry details are provided in documents during due diligence.

risks.title: Every risk is accounted for.
risks.subtitle: Asset-backed ijara — risks are structurally protected:

cards.title: Asset in your name
cards.text: Even if the company closes, the asset is yours — it can be leased to another operator.

cards.title: Ring-fenced project
cards.text: Returns come only from this asset pool's net profit.

cards.title: IoT control
cards.text: Every asset has GPS + remote lock. No payment — no operation.

cards.title: Real network
cards.text: 709 users, a live pilot — not a projection.

cards.title: Islamic finance (Ijarah)
cards.text: Risk-sharing, no riba, asset-backed — an Ijarah structure.

cards.title: Illiquidity risk
cards.text: This investment is illiquid for the 48-month term — an early-exit mechanism is not guaranteed.

cards.title: FX risk (USD)
cards.text: Capital and returns are fixed in UZS; som depreciation reduces USD returns.

cards.title: Regulatory risk
cards.text: Changes in Uzbekistan's financial regulation may affect this structure.

items.a: No — this is profit-share. Returns depend on actual net profit, so we show scenarios (Conservative–Upside) openly. A guaranteed rate would be riba and contrary to Islamic-finance principles.
Physical assets — cabinet, e-bike, battery — in your name. This is asset-backed, not equity.
The asset stays yours. Each has GPS + remote lock — it can be transferred to another operator or sold.
Revenue minus operating costs (swap 45.9%, e-bike service + VAT 22%). Depreciation is borne by the asset owner (you) per AAOIFI, excluded from profit-share.
